intervention_label: BCL-xL-selective inhibitors (A-1155463, A-1331852, WEHI-539) with doxorubicin or cisplatin
target_feature_label: High-grade chondrosarcoma with dedifferentiated features - the apoptotic block that limits chemotherapy
mechanism: BCL-xL holds BAX and BAK in check and keeps chondrosarcoma cells above the threshold at which anthracycline-induced damage would trigger mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilisation. A BH3-mimetic that binds the BCL-xL groove selectively displaces the pro-apoptotic partners and lets a chemotherapy dose that was already being absorbed convert into cell death.
rationale: The upstream chemoresistance work reached ABT-737, a pan-BCL-2/BCL-xL/BCL-w binder, and stopped there. The de Jong dissection goes one step further and says which member actually matters: across eight chondrosarcoma lines, selective BCL-xL blockade produced activity and synergised with doxorubicin or cisplatin in three, while a selective BCL-2 inhibitor did nothing at all. BCL-xL protein also rose with histological grade on a 137-tumour array, which points the finding at the high-grade end of the disease rather than away from it. For a patient whose one real systemic lever is anthracycline chemotherapy, lowering the apoptotic threshold is the most direct way to make that lever work harder.
novelty: No BCL-xL-selective agent has a registered trial in chondrosarcoma, and the upstream preclinical row covers the pan-inhibitor ABT-737 rather than the family-member dissection or any clinical-grade route.

key_manuscripts.finding: Selective BCL-xL inhibition (WEHI-539, A-1155463) killed a subset of eight chondrosarcoma lines and synergised with doxorubicin or cisplatin in three of them, while the BCL-2-selective S55746 was inactive and could not sensitise to chemotherapy. In the orthotopic Swarm rat model, BCL-xL but not BCL-2 inhibition slowed tumour growth.

Class I HDAC inhibition sensitised chondrosarcoma lines to BCL-2-family inhibitors in 2D and 3D, independent of IDH status or subtype, which suggests the apoptotic threshold can be lowered pharmacologically before the BH3 mimetic arrives.

developability: A-1155463, A-1331852 and WEHI-539 are tool compounds with no IND. The clinical-grade path runs through platelet-sparing BCL-xL degraders such as DT2216, which have phase 1 data in other indications; a chondrosarcoma programme would have to be built from scratch.
risks: On-target thrombocytopenia is the reason no BCL-xL-selective small molecule has been developed as a systemic agent
In the rat model BCL-xL inhibition slowed growth on its own but did not sensitise to doxorubicin, so the in-vitro synergy has not reproduced in vivo
Only three of eight lines synergised and no BH3-profiling assay exists to pick the responders prospectively
The cell lines and the tissue array are conventional chondrosarcoma; the dedifferentiated component has not been tested
caveats: The in-vitro-to-in-vivo gap in the anchor paper is the honest weak point, and it sits exactly where the clinical hypothesis lives.

intervention_label: NAMPT inhibitors (FK866/APO866, KPT-9274, OT-82) exploiting NAPRT promoter hypermethylation
target_feature_label: IDH1/IDH2 mutation status - the founder event's downstream methylation debt rather than the enzyme
mechanism: NAD+ can be made from nicotinamide via NAMPT or salvaged from nicotinic acid via NAPRT. When the NAPRT promoter is methylated, the second route is closed and the cell depends entirely on NAMPT, so a NAMPT inhibitor collapses the NAD+ pool and with it glycolysis and PARP-dependent repair.
rationale: This is the shape of vulnerability the case asked for: a consequence of the IDH-driven hypermethylation phenotype that persists whether or not the dedifferentiated clone still needs the mutant enzyme. Peterse and colleagues found low-nanomolar sensitivity in nearly half of eleven chondrosarcoma lines, with sensitivity tracking NAPRT expression and promoter methylation, and explicitly no correlation with IDH1/2 mutation status. The detail that matters for this patient is directional: NAPRT promoter methylation was higher in high-grade than low-grade tumours, so the argument gets stronger rather than weaker at her grade. It also survives the scenario where IDH testing comes back wild-type.
novelty: No NAMPT inhibitor has a registered trial in chondrosarcoma or any sarcoma, and NAD+ depletion appears nowhere in the upstream trial, clinical or preclinical files.

key_manuscripts.finding: Eleven chondrosarcoma lines were treated with NAMPT inhibitors; nearly half had absolute IC50s in the low nanomolar range, with dose-dependent loss of viability, colony formation and 3D collagen invasion. Sensitivity tracked NAPRT expression and promoter methylation, not IDH1/2 mutation status, and NAPRT methylation was higher in high-grade than low-grade tumours.
IDH1-mutant cells lose NAPRT1 expression and become acutely dependent on NAMPT, so NAMPT inhibition depletes NAD+ and kills them selectively, with activity in IDH1-mutant xenografts.

PARG inhibition traps NAD+ in poly(ADP-ribose) chains and deepens the metabolic lethality of alkylating chemotherapy in IDH-mutant tumour cells, which sketches a combination route if single-agent NAD+ depletion is too shallow.

model_systems: genome-wide methylation dataset, 20 IDH1/2-mutant cartilage tumours
developability: FK866 and GMX1778 went through phase 1 in the 2000s and stalled on thrombocytopenia and retinal toxicity without efficacy signals; KPT-9274 and OT-82 are the newer molecules. Any move here needs a NAPRT assay that works on clinical material, which does not exist yet.
risks: The clinical history of NAMPT inhibitors is poor - dose-limiting thrombocytopenia and retinal toxicity, no efficacy signal in unselected phase 1 populations
Dietary or supplemental nicotinic acid rescues NAPRT-competent cells and would blunt the effect in any patient not on a controlled intake
No in-vivo chondrosarcoma data at all; the whole chondrosarcoma case is cell-line work from one group
NAPRT promoter methylation as a selection biomarker has never been run prospectively
caveats: Sensitivity was measured in conventional chondrosarcoma lines; whether a dedifferentiated component keeps the same NAPRT silencing is unknown.

intervention_label: DNMT1-directed hypomethylating therapy (decitabine, guadecitabine) in H3K27me3-deficient dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma
target_feature_label: Dedifferentiated component with PRC2 inactivation - a target inside the transition itself
mechanism: PRC2 loss removes H3K27me3 repression from retrotransposons, and DNA methylation becomes the remaining brake. Inhibiting DNMT1 releases that brake, derepressed retroelements form double-stranded RNA, PKR and the viral-mimicry response fire, and the cell dies. Cells with intact PRC2 keep the histone-mark safeguard and survive the same exposure.
rationale: The case notes that the dedifferentiation transition has no functional model and only descriptive human sequencing. This is the one place where the descriptive work names a druggable consequence: Makise and colleagues found H3K27me3 loss in six of nineteen dedifferentiated chondrosarcomas, confined to the dedifferentiated component while the cartilaginous component retained the mark, with SUZ12 or EED alterations in the dedifferentiated areas only. Patel and colleagues then showed in MPNST, the other PRC2-loss sarcoma, that exactly this state creates a DNMT1 dependency with antitumour response in vivo. The test is cheap and already within reach: H3K27me3 immunohistochemistry on the dedifferentiated component, which the expert pathology review this case already needs could carry.
novelty: No hypomethylating agent has a registered trial in chondrosarcoma, and PRC2 status has never been used to select therapy in a cartilage tumour; the mechanism appears nowhere upstream.

key_manuscripts.finding: An RNAi screen in MPNST showed PRC2 inactivation sensitises to genetic or small-molecule DNMT1 inhibition, with enhanced cytotoxicity and antitumour response driven by retrotransposon derepression and a PKR-dependent viral-mimicry response.

Six of nineteen dedifferentiated chondrosarcomas lost H3K27me3 in the dedifferentiated component while the well-differentiated component retained it; SUZ12 or EED alterations were present in the dedifferentiated areas and absent from the cartilaginous ones.

Polycomb loss reorders the epigenome in MPNST and creates therapeutic vulnerabilities, a second line of evidence that PRC2-null sarcoma cells are pharmacologically distinguishable from PRC2-intact ones.

model_systems: 19 human dedifferentiated chondrosarcomas with paired components
developability: Decitabine and azacitidine are approved and cheap, so the barrier is a biomarker-selected trial rather than a molecule. The selection assay is a single immunohistochemical stain.
risks: The therapeutic data are entirely MPNST; not one chondrosarcoma model has been tested

H3K27me3 loss appeared in about a third of cases and skewed to ribs and the upper half of the body, whereas this patient's lesion is pelvic, which lowers the prior probability before any staining is done
Loss of the histone mark by IHC is not the same as a PRC2 inactivating mutation, and the two can come apart
Myelosuppression from a hypomethylating agent stacks badly with the anthracycline-based chemotherapy this patient is likely to receive
Hypomethylating agents have a long record of disappointing in solid tumours
caveats: Nothing here should delay chemotherapy; the H3K27me3 stain is a parallel question, not a gating one.

intervention_label: Class I HDAC inhibitor priming (vorinostat, romidepsin, entinostat) before BH3-mimetic or glutaminolysis blockade
target_feature_label: High-grade chondrosarcoma with dedifferentiated features - epigenetic control of the apoptotic and metabolic set-point
mechanism: Class I HDACs hold down transcription of BH3-only proteins and shape the metabolic programme chondrosarcoma cells run. Inhibiting them shifts the apoptotic set-point and the metabolic state, so a subsequent BCL-2-family inhibitor or glutaminase inhibitor meets a cell already closer to the death threshold.
rationale: Venneker and colleagues screened epigenetic compounds across five chondrosarcoma lines and found HDAC inhibition was the standout, in both 2D and 3D, and independent of IDH mutation status or subtype - which matters here because this patient's IDH status is unknown. The more useful result is the second one: class I HDAC inhibition made the cells sensitive to Bcl-2-family and glutaminolysis inhibitors that they otherwise tolerated. That makes this a priming strategy that sits underneath two other things already in play for this case, the BCL-xL idea above and the glutaminase inhibitor already surfaced upstream.
novelty: HDAC inhibitors have no chondrosarcoma trial and appear nowhere upstream; the priming combination with a BH3 mimetic has never been taken past cell culture in any cartilage tumour.

key_manuscripts.finding: An epigenetics compound screen across five chondrosarcoma lines found high sensitivity to HDAC inhibition in 2D and 3D regardless of IDH status or subtype, with dependence on multiple class I HDACs, and class I inhibition sensitised the cells to glutaminolysis and Bcl-2-family inhibitors.
Vorinostat and panobinostat produced G1 arrest and apoptosis in multidrug-resistant sarcoma lines, including chondrosarcoma, suggesting HDAC inhibition is not simply undone by the efflux phenotype.

HDAC inhibitors pushed chondrosarcoma cells toward differentiation rather than pure cytotoxicity, an older observation that fits the idea of HDACs setting a cell-state rather than acting as a straightforward killer.

model_systems: five human chondrosarcoma cell lines, 2D and 3D
siRNA knockdown of individual HDAC isoforms
developability: Vorinostat and romidepsin are approved in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, so a repurposing combination trial needs no new chemistry. The obstacle is a phase 1 combination whose two arms share the same dose-limiting toxicity.
risks: Thrombocytopenia from a class I HDAC inhibitor and thrombocytopenia from a BCL-xL agent are the same dose-limiting toxicity, which is a genuine problem for the exact combination this row proposes
HDAC inhibitors have repeatedly failed as single agents in solid tumours including sarcoma
All chondrosarcoma evidence is cell culture; no animal work and no dedifferentiated models
Priming schedules are notoriously sensitive to sequence and interval, none of which has been worked out here
caveats: On its own this is unlikely to do much; the value is entirely in what it enables.

intervention_label: Plectin inhibition with Plecstatin-1 in dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma
target_feature_label: Dedifferentiated component - cytolinker-dependent migration and EMT
mechanism: Plectin cross-links intermediate filaments to actin and to focal adhesions and is a common dependency in migratory, mesenchymal-state tumour cells. Plecstatin-1, a ruthenium organometallic compound, binds plectin and disrupts that scaffold; in the reported DDCS line the downstream effect ran through AKT/ERK signalling with loss of migration, invasion and EMT markers.
rationale: Almost nothing in the chondrosarcoma literature is generated in a genuinely dedifferentiated model, which is the gap this case flagged. PUMC-DDCS1 is a newly established patient-derived DDCS line with matched multi-omics, 100% tumorigenicity in NOD/SCID mice, and drug sensitivity to cisplatin and doxorubicin - a useful internal control, since it reproduces the chemosensitivity that makes this histology different. Within that model, plectin inhibition was the one non-cytotoxic hit. It is a thin result and I would not read it as more than a hypothesis, but it is the only compound nomination in this scan that came out of a dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma model rather than being imported into one.
novelty: Plecstatin-1 is an academic organometallic tool compound with no IND and no oncology development programme in any indication.

key_manuscripts.finding: PUMC-DDCS1, a new patient-derived dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma line with matched whole-genome, exome, bisulfite and transcriptome profiling, was sensitive to cisplatin, doxorubicin and Plecstatin-1 and resistant to methotrexate; plectin inhibition suppressed migration, invasion and EMT, apparently through AKT/ERK.

model_systems: PUMC-DDCS1 patient-derived dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma cell line
developability: Tool compound only. There is no clinical-grade plectin inhibitor, no toxicology package, and ruthenium organometallics carry their own formulation and exposure problems.
risks: Single unreplicated preprint, not peer reviewed
One cell line, and the anti-plectin effect was measured on migration and invasion rather than on survival or tumour burden
Plectin is broadly expressed in skin, muscle and epithelia, so on-target toxicity is a live question with no data
No in-vivo efficacy work at all
caveats: The line itself may be worth more to this field than the compound is.

intervention_label: 5'-methylschweinfurthin G (MeSG), an academic natural-product analogue active in matrix-rich chondrosarcoma
target_feature_label: Cartilaginous matrix and drug penetration in a bulky high-grade lesion
mechanism: Schweinfurthins act on oxysterol-binding-protein-family lipid transfer proteins and disturb cholesterol and sphingolipid trafficking, a dependency that some tumour lineages have and normal cells largely do not. The chondrosarcoma work reports a roughly 300-fold potency window between tumour cells and freshly isolated chondrocytes, which is the more interesting number.
rationale: This compound was developed explicitly against the problem the case raises - a hyaline-cartilage-like, collagen II and proteoglycan-rich tumour that resists drug penetration. In the Swarm rat chondrosarcoma, which carries exactly that matrix phenotype, repeated dosing cut tumour mass by 83% and eliminated tumour in three of ten animals, with reduced proliferation and increased cell death on histology. That is a real in-vivo result in the right matrix context, and it stands almost alone in a literature where matrix-directed ideas have not moved.
novelty: Academic natural-product analogue with no IND, no company programme and no registered trial in any indication.

key_manuscripts.finding: MeSG had an IC50 of 35 nM against Swarm rat chondrosarcoma cells versus 11 uM for freshly isolated rat chondrocytes; repeated 20 mg/kg dosing reduced tumour mass by 83% over 17 days with complete elimination in three of ten mice.

model_systems: primary rat chondrocytes as the selectivity comparator
developability: No IND, no pharmacokinetics, no formal toxicology. Schweinfurthin chemistry is synthetically demanding and the target engagement mechanism is still argued over, so this needs the full preclinical package before anyone could think about a patient.
risks: One paper from one group in 2018 with no independent replication and no visible follow-up
Rat chondrosarcoma with a well-differentiated cartilage phenotype, which is close to the matrix problem but far from a dedifferentiated human tumour
The OSBP/ORP4 mechanism is inferred from the schweinfurthin class rather than demonstrated here
Systemic cholesterol-trafficking disruption has unexplored toxicity
caveats: I have listed this because it is real in-vivo activity in the right matrix context, not because anyone is close to dosing a person with it.

intervention_label: Anti-miR-181a oligonucleotide delivered on a nanopiece platform
target_feature_label: Multiple dispersed pulmonary metastases - the angiogenic and invasive programme driving them
mechanism: miR-181a is overexpressed in high-grade chondrosarcoma and represses RGS16, which normally dampens CXCR4 signalling. Sequestering the miRNA restores RGS16, quiets CXCR4, and lowers MMP1 and VEGF output, hitting angiogenesis and invasion rather than proliferation.
rationale: Systemic control of the lungs is the operative question in this case, and the local approaches are closed off by the number and distribution of the nodules. Sun and colleagues delivered anti-miR-181a systemically in chondrosarcoma xenografts and got a 32% reduction in tumour volume and survival improving from 23% to 45%, with the expected molecular readouts. The effect size is modest and the work is one group's, but it is a genuinely different modality against a metastasis-directed mechanism, and nothing in this class appears upstream.
novelty: Academic oligonucleotide plus an unlicensed delivery platform; no IND and no trial in any indication.

key_manuscripts.finding: Systemically delivered anti-miR-181a on a nanopiece carrier transfected chondrosarcoma xenografts, restored RGS16, lowered VEGF, MMP1 and MMP activity, cut tumour volume 32% by day 38 and raised survival from 23% to 45%.

model_systems: human chondrosarcoma xenografts in nude mice
developability: Both the oligonucleotide and the nanopiece carrier are academic. Oligonucleotide chemistry is a solved problem in principle, but this specific delivery platform has no regulatory history and no toxicology.
risks: A 32% volume reduction is a modest effect and would not on its own justify a trial
Single laboratory, no independent replication
miR-181a expression in this patient's tumour is unknown and there is no clinical assay for it
Subcutaneous xenografts say little about whether the agent reaches established pulmonary metastases
caveats: The metastasis-directed endpoint is the appealing part; the delivery platform is the part that would take years.

intervention_label: Blocking the interstitial-shear to MMP-7/MMP-12 axis (IGF-2, VEGF-B/D, IL-1beta or MMP-7/12 as nodes)
target_feature_label: Large acetabular lesion with pathologic fracture - the mechanical environment as a driver, not just a complication
mechanism: Interstitial fluid flow across chondrosarcoma cells raises cAMP and IL-1beta and induces IGF-2 and VEGF-B/D, which transactivate MMP-7 and MMP-12 through PI3K, ERK, p38 and JNK. The resulting proteases drive motility, matrix invasion and, in the mouse, lung colonisation. Interrupting any node in that chain is the strategy; none has a clinical-grade selective agent.
rationale: The case flagged that nothing translatable exists on tumour biology at a fractured, loaded site. That is broadly right, but it is not quite empty. Wang, Guan and colleagues built the mechanical arm in human chondrosarcoma lines and showed the shear-induced MMP programme is sufficient to promote lung colonisation in vivo, which links a mechanical input to precisely the two features that dominate this case - a load-bearing pelvic lesion and disseminated pulmonary nodules. Fan and colleagues add the uncomfortable half of the picture from a breast-cancer osteolysis model: loading is not monotonically good or bad, with low-intensity load suppressing osteolysis and higher intensity reversing the benefit. That is a caution about weight-bearing and rehabilitation decisions as much as a drug target.
novelty: No selective MMP-7 or MMP-12 agent exists in development, and no trial in any indication targets mechanically induced invasion; the mechanism appears nowhere upstream.

key_manuscripts.finding: Fluid shear at 2 dyn/cm2 upregulated MMP-12 in human chondrosarcoma cells via IGF-2 and VEGF-B/D through PI3K, p38 and JNK; MMP-12 overexpression potentiated invasion in vitro and lung colonisation in vivo.
In SW1353, HS.819.T and CH2879 cells, shear-induced cAMP and IL-1beta drove MMP-7 synthesis through NF-kB and c-Jun, and MMP-7 upregulation promoted chondrosarcoma lung colonisation in vivo.

Tibial loading at 1 N suppressed tumour-induced osteolysis while 2 N and 5 N loading lost and then reversed that benefit, with osteocyte-derived signals switching cells between mesenchymal and epithelial states depending on flow intensity.

model_systems: human chondrosarcoma lines SW1353, HS.819.T, CH2879 under controlled fluid shear
murine tibial loading model of tumour-induced osteolysis (breast cancer)
developability: There is no drug here. Broad-spectrum MMP inhibitors were abandoned in the 1990s for musculoskeletal toxicity without efficacy, and nobody has built a selective MMP-7 or MMP-12 agent for oncology. The upstream nodes (IGF-2, VEGF-B/D) have agents but none has been tested against this readout.
risks: The MMP-inhibitor field has a bad history and a selective agent would be starting from zero
The link from this patient's pathologic fracture and altered load to the shear stresses used in the bioreactor is an inference, not a measurement
The loading-intensity data come from a breast-cancer osteolysis model, not a cartilage tumour
Blocking matrix proteolysis could plausibly worsen drug penetration in a matrix-dense tumour, which cuts against the matrix-normalisation ideas elsewhere in this file
caveats: Read this as target biology worth measuring in her tumour rather than as an intervention anyone can offer.

intervention_label: Blocking the collagen-LAIR-1 inhibitory axis in a collagen II-rich tumour (LAIR-2-Fc or equivalent)
target_feature_label: Dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma immune microenvironment - collagen as an active immunosuppressive ligand
mechanism: LAIR-1 is an ITIM-bearing inhibitory receptor on T cells, NK cells, monocytes and dendritic cells whose physiological ligand is collagen. Engagement suppresses effector function; a soluble LAIR-2 decoy or a blocking antibody competes collagen away from LAIR-1 and lifts that brake.
rationale: The upstream immunology in this case pointed at collagen and myeloid infiltration as the operative resistance mechanisms rather than T-cell exhaustion, and at the myeloid compartment as the better lever. LAIR-1 is the one receptor that ties those two observations into a single mechanism, and the detail that makes it worth writing down is that Lebbink and colleagues mapped multiple high-affinity LAIR binding sites specifically on collagens II and III. Collagen II is the defining matrix protein of a cartilage tumour. Peng and colleagues separately showed collagen drives anti-PD-1 resistance through LAIR1-dependent CD8 exhaustion, which would explain checkpoint failure in this disease better than PD-L1 levels do. I want to be blunt: nobody has looked at LAIR-1 in a cartilage tumour, so this is a hypothesis about why the existing immunotherapy story is disappointing, not a treatment.
novelty: LAIR-1 has never been examined in chondrosarcoma or any cartilage tumour, and no collagen-LAIR-directed programme exists in sarcoma of any type.

key_manuscripts.finding: Mapped multiple potent LAIR-1 and LAIR-2 binding sites on collagens II and III, establishing that the cartilage-defining collagen is a high-affinity ligand for the inhibitory receptor.
Tumour collagen drove resistance to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade through LAIR1-dependent CD8+ T-cell exhaustion, and blocking the axis restored response in murine models.
Collagens expressed by tumours were sufficient to inhibit immune cell function through LAIR-1, showing the ligand does not need to come from stroma.
NC410, a LAIR-2 Fc fusion, blocked human LAIR-collagen interaction, remodelled collagen and improved T-cell infiltration and antitumour immunity in humanised models.

developability: A clinical-grade LAIR-2-Fc (NC410) exists and has been dosed in solid-tumour trials in other histologies, so if the target validated in chondrosarcoma the molecule would not have to be invented. The missing step is entirely at the target-validation end: LAIR-1 staining on chondrosarcoma tumour-infiltrating myeloid and T cells, which nobody has done.
risks: Zero data in cartilage tumours; the mechanistic fit is inferred from collagen II biochemistry

Releasing LAIR-1 inhibition on monocytes could as easily amplify a tumour-supportive myeloid programme as an antitumour one, and the syngeneic chondrosarcoma data already show macrophage depletion helping rather than macrophage activation
Collagen II in chondrosarcoma is often abnormal, and whether it retains the LAIR-binding motifs is unknown
The clinical-grade agent's activity in other tumours has been modest
caveats: This belongs on a correlative-science list before it belongs on a therapy list.

intervention_label: Targeting the SOX9-to-RUNX2 differentiation switch that defines the dedifferentiated component
mechanism: SOX9 maintains the chondrocytic programme and RUNX2 drives the osteoblastic and mesenchymal one; dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma lines carry the opposite balance to conventional lines. The strategy is either to re-impose the SOX9 programme on the dedifferentiated clone or to attack a dependency that only the RUNX2-high state has - neither of which currently has a molecule.
rationale: This is the honest answer to whether anything nominates a target inside the transition. Almost nothing does. What exists is Tang's observation that SOX9 and RUNX2 expression separate conventional from dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma lines, and Stoeckl's functional result that knocking SOX9 out of a chondrosarcoma line changes ploidy and shifts sensitivity to standard treatment modalities - so the differentiation state is not merely descriptive, it moves the drug response. Nicolle's multi-omic classification then puts a balance between differentiation and cell-cycle activation at the centre of chondrosarcoma subtyping. Together that is enough to say the axis is real and enough to say nobody has drugged it.
novelty: No compound targets this axis in any indication; SOX9 and RUNX2 are transcription factors with no clinical-grade ligands and no degrader programmes.

key_manuscripts.finding: SOX9 knockout in a chondrosarcoma line induced polyploidy and altered sensitivity to standard tumour treatment strategies, showing the chondrogenic transcription programme actively shapes drug response.
Conventional and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma lines carried opposite SOX9 and RUNX2 expression patterns, marking the transcriptional axis that separates the two components.

Multi-omic profiling split chondrosarcoma into two subtypes defined by the balance between tumour differentiation and cell-cycle activation, with the classification predicting outcome and behaving progressively in relapsed samples.
Established two dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma cell lines alongside a grade III conventional line, the small stock of models any functional work on the transition would have to use.

model_systems: chondrosarcoma cell lines with SOX9 knockout
paired conventional and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma lines
developability: Nothing to develop yet. The realistic first step is a functional model of the transition - the field has perhaps a handful of dedifferentiated lines and no genetically engineered mouse - followed by a screen against the RUNX2-high state.
risks: Direction of benefit is unclear: forcing redifferentiation might restore the chemoresistant cartilage phenotype rather than help
SOX9 knockout produced polyploidy, which is not obviously a therapeutic outcome
Transcription factors of this class have no tractable chemistry
All of the human evidence is correlative
caveats: I include this to name the gap precisely rather than to propose a treatment.

intervention_label: Biomarker-selected SMO inhibition (vismodegib) in PTCH1-altered chondrosarcoma, nominated by patient-derived organoids
target_feature_label: Unmeasured molecular landscape - PTCH1 loss-of-function as a selection marker
mechanism: PTCH1 normally restrains SMO; loss-of-function releases that restraint and the hedgehog pathway signals constitutively. Vismodegib binds SMO and shuts the pathway down, which only helps in tumours where the lesion sits upstream of SMO.
rationale: Hedgehog inhibition in chondrosarcoma has a bad name, and it earned it in an unselected phase 2 (NCT01310816) that went nowhere. The Takami preprint is interesting because it changes the selection question rather than the drug: the first patient-derived chondrosarcoma organoids, validated against their parental tumours histologically and genetically, carried PTCH1 loss-of-function and responded strongly to vismodegib in vitro. That is a genotype-selected version of a hypothesis that previously failed unselected. Since this patient has had no genomic profiling at all, PTCH1 would come along free on any comprehensive panel already needed for the IDH question.
novelty: No genotype-selected hedgehog trial exists in chondrosarcoma; the prior chondrosarcoma programme was unselected and did not advance, and the organoid nomination is unpublished.

key_manuscripts.finding: Two patient-derived chondrosarcoma organoid lines grown at an air-liquid interface preserved parental histology and genetics in NOD-SCID xenografts; whole-exome profiling found PTCH1 and BCOR loss-of-function, and vismodegib had strong in-vitro antitumour activity.

model_systems: organoid-derived xenografts in NOD-SCID IL2Rg-null mice
whole-exome profiling of organoid and parental tumour
developability: Vismodegib and sonidegib are approved, so this is a selection problem rather than a chemistry problem. What is missing is any evidence that PTCH1 alterations occur at usable frequency in chondrosarcoma, which two organoid lines cannot establish.
risks: Unselected hedgehog inhibition already failed in advanced chondrosarcoma, and the burden of proof on any revival is high
Two organoid lines, preprint, no peer review, no in-vivo drug treatment reported
PTCH1 loss-of-function is not a recognised recurrent event in chondrosarcoma genomic series, so the prior is low
The organoids are not described as dedifferentiated, and the activity was in vitro only
SMO inhibitor toxicity - muscle cramps, alopecia, dysgeusia - is poorly tolerated over months in a patient already at ECOG 2
caveats: The value here is mostly that patient-derived chondrosarcoma organoids now exist; the vismodegib nomination is the thinner half of the paper.

intervention_label: Losartan or other antifibrotic matrix normalisation to improve drug delivery into cartilaginous tumour
target_feature_label: Matrix-mediated chemoresistance in a bulky cartilaginous mass
mechanism: Angiotensin receptor blockade suppresses TGF-beta and CCN2 signalling in stromal fibroblasts, reduces collagen I and hyaluronan deposition, lowers solid stress, decompresses vessels and lets more chemotherapy reach the tumour interior. The logic is delivery, not cytotoxicity.
rationale: I looked hard for anything that had moved past the hyaluronidase failure and found nothing in cartilage tumours. Losartan is the strongest repurposing candidate in the general matrix-normalisation literature, with reduced collagen, improved perfusion and better chemotherapy efficacy in ovarian and pancreatic models. But I want to be honest about the mismatch: that work targets CAF-derived collagen I and hyaluronan, whereas the chondrosarcoma barrier is tumour-cell-made collagen II and aggrecan laid down by the malignant chondrocytes themselves, which is a different problem with a different enzyme set. This row is here because the question deserved an answer, and the answer is that the field has not built the right tool.
novelty: No matrix-normalisation agent has ever been tested in a cartilage tumour, in any model or any trial.

key_manuscripts.finding: Losartan normalised the tumour stroma in ovarian cancer models, reduced collagen and solid stress, improved chemotherapy efficacy and reduced ascites - the clearest of the antifibrotic delivery results, in a tumour type unrelated to this case.

model_systems: murine and orthotopic ovarian cancer models
developability: Losartan is generic, oral and cheap, so a delivery-endpoint study would be inexpensive. The prerequisite is a chondrosarcoma model with a measurable penetration readout, which the 3D pellet systems could provide but nobody has run.
risks: Mechanism mismatch: cartilage matrix is collagen II and aggrecan, not the CAF-derived collagen I that losartan acts on
The PEGPH20 experience is a warning that improving delivery on paper does not improve outcomes and can worsen them
Hypotension in a patient with ECOG 2 and a painful pathologic fracture is not a trivial side effect
Loosening a matrix that is physically containing tumour has an obvious theoretical downside nobody has excluded
caveats: Included as the honest answer to a direct question, not because I think it is close to testable here.

intervention_label: Nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates (zoledronic acid, minodronate) as antitumour agents in the bone niche
target_feature_label: Large acetabular lesion with pathologic fracture - the osteolytic bone niche
mechanism: Nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates block farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase, disable osteoclasts and interrupt the resorption-driven release of bone-matrix growth factors that feeds tumour at a skeletal site. Direct effects on tumour-cell invasion and MMP-2 secretion have also been reported in chondrosarcoma lines.
rationale: The Swarm rat model is the only in-vivo evidence that anything slows chondrosarcoma at a bone site: zoledronic acid slowed primary tumour development, slowed recurrence after intralesional curettage and improved overall survival. That combination - primary growth plus post-curettage recurrence - maps unusually well onto a large acetabular lesion where local control is contested. The supporting cell work adds a direct anti-invasive effect on chondrosarcoma cells rather than a purely osteoclast-mediated one.
novelty: No bisphosphonate has ever been trialled as antitumour therapy in chondrosarcoma; the twenty-year-old rat result was never taken forward.

key_manuscripts.finding: Zoledronic acid slowed primary Swarm rat chondrosarcoma development, slowed recurrent tumour progression after intralesional curettage, and increased overall survival.
Alendronate inhibited invasion and MMP-2 secretion in a human chondrosarcoma line, pointing at a tumour-cell-directed effect alongside the osteoclast one.

model_systems: orthotopic Swarm rat chondrosarcoma with intralesional curettage
human chondrosarcoma cell line invasion assays
developability: Generic and already used in oncology, so the molecule is not the obstacle. The obstacle is designing a study that can separate an antitumour effect from the skeletal-related-event benefit these drugs already provide.
risks: Zoledronic acid added to chemotherapy failed to improve outcomes in the OS2006 osteosarcoma trial, the closest clinical read-through available
Osteonecrosis of the jaw and atypical femoral fracture matter more, not less, in a patient with an existing pathologic fracture of a weight-bearing joint
The efficacy evidence is a rat model from 2006 with no replication
Bisphosphonate or denosumab use for skeletal-related events is separately standard supportive care, so any antitumour claim is hard to isolate and this row should not be read as duplicating that
caveats: The supportive-care indication is a different conversation and belongs to the standard-of-care track; this row is only about the antitumour hypothesis.

intervention_label: Venetoclax (BCL-2-selective) in chondrosarcoma
mechanism: Venetoclax occupies the BCL-2 BH3 groove selectively and spares BCL-xL and MCL-1.
rationale: Venetoclax is the obvious clinical-grade way to act on the apoptotic block that the upstream ABT-737 work identified, so I checked it directly.
exclusion_reason: Set aside because the chondrosarcoma data argue against it specifically: de Jong and colleagues (PMID 30242253) tested the BCL-2-selective S55746 across eight chondrosarcoma lines and found no activity and no chemosensitisation, while BCL-xL-selective agents worked. BCL-2 is the wrong family member here, and the BCL-xL row carries this idea forward.

intervention_label: DT2216, platelet-sparing BCL-xL PROTAC degrader
mechanism: A VHL-recruiting PROTAC that degrades BCL-xL in tumour cells while sparing platelets, which lack sufficient VHL.
rationale: The natural clinical-grade route for the BCL-xL dependency this scan surfaced.
exclusion_reason: Already clinical-stage and therefore trial_screener's territory: a phase 1 has completed (NCT04886622) and further studies are recruiting (NCT06964009, NCT06620302). Named in the developability field of the BCL-xL row instead of logged as a separate horizon candidate.

intervention_label: INBRX-109, tetravalent DR5 agonist antibody
mechanism: Multivalent DR5 clustering triggers the extrinsic apoptotic pathway, an alternative route around the same apoptotic block as the BH3 mimetics.
rationale: Death-receptor agonism has a long chondrosarcoma preclinical history and would otherwise be a strong horizon candidate.
exclusion_reason: Already surfaced as a clinical-stage drug by trial_screener's remit: a randomised phase 2 in conventional chondrosarcoma is active (NCT04950075) with preclinical and phase 1 data published (PMID 37265425). Worth flagging that the registered study is in conventional, not dedifferentiated, chondrosarcoma.

intervention_label: Disulfiram plus copper as a chondrosarcoma stem-cell radiosensitiser
mechanism: The disulfiram-copper complex inhibits ALDH and the proteasome pathway in ALDH+CD133+ chondrosarcoma stem cells, which are the fraction that survives fractionated irradiation.
rationale: Directly relevant to local control of the acetabular lesion, with orthotopic in-vivo radiosensitisation data (PMID 33582212).
exclusion_reason: Already clinical-stage in sarcoma and so belongs to trial_screener: disulfiram with copper gluconate and liposomal doxorubicin is recruiting in refractory sarcoma (NCT05210374). The radiosensitisation combination specifically has no trial, but the agent is past the horizon boundary.

intervention_label: CSF1R inhibitors (pexidartinib, vimseltinib) against the tumour-associated macrophage compartment
mechanism: CSF1R blockade depletes or reprograms CSF1R-dependent tumour-associated macrophages.
rationale: The syngeneic chondrosarcoma data showing CD163+ macrophage depletion slows growth make this the most mechanistically supported immune approach in the case.
exclusion_reason: Named already by the upstream layers and now clinical-stage in sarcoma: a phase 1 of vimseltinib with avelumab in advanced sarcoma has reported (PMID 40714516) and pexidartinib is approved in tenosynovial giant cell tumour. Out of scope here as a result, though no chondrosarcoma-specific study exists.

intervention_label: CD47/SIRPalpha blockade as an alternative myeloid lever
mechanism: Blocking the CD47 don't-eat-me signal licenses macrophage phagocytosis of tumour cells.
rationale: The obvious candidate when asked what else is being built against the myeloid compartment in sarcoma.
exclusion_reason: Set aside as too thin for this tumour: a Europe PMC search returned zero chondrosarcoma or cartilage-tumour publications on CD47, and the one soft-tissue-sarcoma study (PMID 35986756) found CD47 blockade activated immune cells but did not potentiate anti-PD-1. Nothing to anchor a chondrosarcoma hypothesis on, and it would also push macrophages in the opposite direction to the depletion result the upstream syngeneic model reported.

intervention_label: MTAP-deletion-directed PRMT5/MAT2A inhibition
mechanism: CDKN2A deletion frequently co-deletes MTAP, MTA accumulates, and MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors or MAT2A inhibitors become selectively lethal.
rationale: CDKN2A loss is recurrent in high-grade and dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma, so the co-deletion biomarker is plausibly present here.
exclusion_reason: Already clinical-stage across solid tumours in MTAP-deleted basket studies, which puts it in trial_screener's remit rather than this horizon scan. Flagging it anyway because MTAP status would come free on the comprehensive panel this case already needs.

intervention_label: Newly designed targeted hypoxia-activated prodrugs for chondrosarcoma
mechanism: Bioreductive prodrugs that release a cytotoxic warhead only in the severely hypoxic core characteristic of cartilaginous tumours.
rationale: Chondrosarcoma is avascular and profoundly hypoxic, which makes it close to an ideal hypoxia-activated-prodrug substrate.
exclusion_reason: Mechanism already covered upstream: preclinical_evidence.jsonl carries the TH-302 (evofosfamide) hypoxic spheroid row, and the newer academic analogues act by the same bioreductive mechanism without adding an independent line of evidence.

intervention_label: TEAD inhibition in ATRX-deficient sarcoma
mechanism: ATRX loss de-represses chromatin, enriches PRDM4 and NFIX motifs and raises YAP1 dependency, which a TEAD palmitoylation-site inhibitor such as VT103 exploits.
rationale: A recent bioRxiv preprint nominates it across several sarcoma types with a clean mechanism.
exclusion_reason: Set aside on case match: the preprint covers leiomyosarcoma, undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma and dedifferentiated liposarcoma, with no chondrosarcoma in the cohort, and ATRX loss is not a described recurrent event in cartilage tumours. Too far from this patient's histology to carry forward.
